full_judgment: 13. It is now well settled that a procedural law always takes effect retrospectively. In this connection, reliance may be made on the case of Abdul Kader Mirza vs Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs 56 DLR 31 in which it is held that Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, being a procedural law, there is no bar to giving its effect retrospectively and moreso, by the Ain, there is no difference in awarding sentence. It is also held that the Ain is not ultra vires of the Constitution. The aforesaid findings of the High Court Division were approved by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal Nos. 143-145 of 2003 by its judgment dated 9-12-2007. The Appellate Division, however, allowed Civil Appeal No. 144 of 2003 in which the direction of this Division in respect of disposal of Sessions Case No. 11 of 2003 was set aside.
